found: Painted render with grime streaks running down from the top, paint flaking to a grey patch on the left, and one hairline crack. The paint colour and the flaking read as a wall that has been out in the weather. No lettering, numeral, logo, badge, signature or watermark, and no fixing, downpipe or window reveal that would tie it to a particular building. It carries one defect, traced after the first look: a dark band three pixels tall crossing the full width at row 616, 48 grey levels below the tile's own median, dashed. It is not painted content and not third-party content. The dash period along it is exactly 8.0 px (128 cycles across the tile, 21.6 grey levels, the strongest period in that line), which is the autoencoder's own latent cell pitch, and the band is centred exactly on a latent row boundary (616 = 8 x 77). It is neutral dark in all three channels, it is absent from the conditioning picture the model was given, and it appears in 1 of the session's 64 outputs. So it arose inside this lane's own latent pipeline. Which stage is not settled: the roll-boundary explanation tested null across the 64 outputs (47 per cent of strong lines sit on a boundary the seed's schedule visited, against 44 per cent expected by chance), and the latents were not retained, so closing it needs per-latent-row statistics recorded during a run. The set is not offered while the defect stands.
statement: Every texel of every map is inside exactly one of these crops, each written at 1:1 with no resampling, and each was looked at before this set was offered for publication.
